content.text:
## Review complete

I read all changed files and traced the only logic changes (URL params in `stylist.tsx`, back-button fallback in `outfit-detail.tsx`). Every other diff is a pure CSS class swap (`screen-top`, safe-area insets) with no data flow.

**Data-flow verdict on the two logic changes:**

1. **`stylist.tsx` URL param reads** — both attacker-influenceable via query string:
   - `occasion`: gated through `OCCASIONS.find(o => o === sp.get("occasion")) ?? null` — strict whitelist ("everyday" | "work" | "weekend" | "evening"), so only a validated `UiOccasion` reaches state and `defaultReason()`.
   - `look`: `Number(sp.get("look")) || null`, then clamped by `Math.min(desired ?? 0, Math.max(res.looks.length - 1, 0))` before `setSelectedLook`. Only ever used as an array index into `looks[]`. A negative or `Infinity` input just produces a nonsense UI state; no sink reached.
   - Writes use `URLSearchParams.toString()` (auto-encoded) piped into `history.replaceState(null, "", "?" + qs)` — same-origin relative URL, no `javascript:` surface possible from a `?`-prefixed value.

2. **`outfit-detail.tsx` back-button** — `router.push("/generate")` is a static literal. `window.history.length > 1` is a boolean check, no injection.

No shell/SQL/eval/FS/deserialization/HTML/SSRF/authz/PII-logging sinks are touched. No new server actions, no new API surface. The registry-fanout and gate-parity heuristics don't apply — nothing security-relevant is added or removed.
